strengths: Systematic bottom-up approach to investigating minimal necessary optimizer components, with clear methodology and trust-region framework unifying gradient normalizations
Strong empirical results across model scales (60M-7B): achieves 35-45% of Adam's memory while matching performance, outperforming memory-efficient baselines (GaLore, Fira, APOLLO)

Well-motivated design choices with clear evidence: Figure 3 demonstrates output layer variance peaks, Table 2 systematically compares normalizations, Theorem 2.1 justifies layer-wise momentum allocation
Practical and implementable: Algorithm 1 requires minimal modifications to standard implementations, avoiding complex components like SVD or low-rank projections
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: proper hyperparameter search, multiple model scales, learning rate sensitivity analysis, detailed memory estimation, good ablation studies in Tables 2-3
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and well-organized content; Table 4 provides excellent summary of related methods
weaknesses: Limited novelty: column-wise normalization from Pethick et al. (2025), layer-wise momentum is natural extension of prior work; distinction from concurrent work is subtle (last-layer only vs. all-but-last momentum)

Theory-practice gap: Theorem 2.1 analyzes vanilla SGD-M without column normalization; standard O(1/√T) convergence rate doesn't explain why SCALE matches Adam; theorem doesn't capture crucial normalization-momentum interaction

Narrow evaluation scope: limited to LLaMA models on C4 dataset; no evaluation on other architectures, datasets, sequence lengths, or downstream tasks; only single 7B run due to computational constraints; SWAN results copied from paper rather than reproduced
Incomplete generalization analysis: unclear if SCALE works for different sequence lengths, very large models (70B+), fine-tuning scenarios, or other precisions beyond BF16

Experimental design concerns: vector parameters still use Adam (hybrid approach complicates minimalist narrative); gradient variance estimated with batch size 512 vs. training batch 32; learning rates require tuning across model sizes (1e-3, 2e-4, 1e-4)

Missing practical analysis: no wall-clock training time comparisons despite claims of efficiency; no numerical stability analysis; memory savings (2% over SGD for 7B) may be modest compared to other modern optimizations

Theoretical exposition issues: Theorem 2.1 contains many opaque constants; connection between theory (ignoring normalization) and practice (critically dependent on normalization) not established; Remark 2.1's explanation somewhat hand-wavy

strengths: Well-motivated research question with systematic bottom-up investigation of minimum SGD modifications needed for SOTA performance

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across model scales (60M-7B) with extensive ablations (Tables 2, 3, 12) and supplementary experiments (architecture diversity, overtraining, fine-tuning, learning rate sensitivity)
Theoretical support via Theorem 2.1 extending momentum convergence analysis to multi-layer settings with heterogeneous variance, justifying layer-selective momentum design
Insightful analysis of last-layer column-wise normalization (A.9, Figure 7) connecting to token frequency imbalance and class imbalance in transformer training
Practical simplicity with minimal code changes and no expensive operations (avoids SVD), making the method easily deployable
Clear progression from component analysis to final algorithm with well-organized presentation and honest discussion of design choices
weaknesses: Limited theoretical novelty: Theorem 2.1 straightforwardly extends Liu et al. (2020) to multi-layer case; crucially, the theory does not explain why normalization helps compared to vanilla SGD (acknowledged by authors)
Core techniques are not novel: column-wise normalization discussed in Pethick et al. (2025), selective momentum used in SWAN. Main contribution is the specific combination, which is incremental

Critical experimental gaps: (1) Only single training run for 7B model with no error bars or statistical significance testing; (2) Memory estimates are theoretical (A.1) rather than measured; (3) Baseline tuning consistency unclear—Fira/APOLLO required learning rate reduction to prevent divergence
Variance estimation method (Section 2.2) uses larger batch sizes (512 vs. 32) to approximate 'true gradient' but lacks validation; relationship to actual training dynamics unclear

Incomplete ablations: No systematic exploration of applying momentum to multiple high-variance layers; β=0.9 choice not justified or ablated; learning rate selection for 1B/7B described as 'manually tune' without details
Narrow experimental scope: Pretraining-only (fine-tuning acknowledgedly not the target), C4 dataset only, single sequence length (256), no evaluation on downstream tasks or domain-specific corpora
Inconsistent baseline comparisons: Some results taken from other papers (SWAN, APOLLO) rather than reproduced; 7B results missing GaLore/Fira; SWAN uses different token budget (13B vs. 20B standard)
Missing reproducibility artifacts: Code availability not mentioned; hyperparameter selection process unclear; learning rate values scattered across appendices; no mention of artifact release
